display.title: Shlomo HaMelech's Pool, Part 1
display.summary_short: A jealous advisor tricks the king into ordering Rabbi Yehuda to build a pool like Shlomo HaMelech's, then plots to have him put to death.
display.summary_long: In a faraway city in Spain, the great scholar Rabbi Yehuda is the king's trusted chief advisor. The jealous advisor Ivan, who hates the Jews, persuades the king to have Rabbi Yehuda build a pool like the famous pool of Shlomo HaMelech, a job no one could do alone. Rabbi Yehuda says Tehillim, and his wife Sarah remembers her late father's chest of building plans. By the light of one candle they make their way through a secret basement and tunnel and find the plans just as the candle goes out. The pool is dug and decorated, but the gold paint keeps floating to the top of the water. Rabbi Yehuda cleverly hands the painting job to Ivan, who secretly knows the trick, and the king is delighted. Ivan then has the king demand an oath that nothing was taken from the treasury. Rabbi Yehuda will not swear to what he cannot know for sure, and he is thrown into the river. A Jewish doctor, Rabbi Yitzchak, rescues and revives him, but keeps him hidden in his home, away from the king. To be continued.
display.lesson: Turn to Hashem with Tehillim when trouble comes, and never swear to something you are not completely sure of.

advisories.note: Rabbi Yehuda is sentenced to death, tied up and thrown into a river; a doctor rescues and revives him.
